grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or plain staple: potatoes, chard, eggs, smoked haddock, crème fraîche, cheddar, lemon and dill.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including smoked haddock and chard, is an everyday item at Tesco or similar.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only an ovenproof frying pan with a lid, a bowl and a whisk, and starting a frittata on the hob then baking it is beginner-friendly.

works.reason: Eight eggs, 400g potatoes, 300g chard and 300g haddock make a generous frittata for four, the potatoes have time to soften, the fish cooks through in the bake, and a pinch of salt suits the salty haddock.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five minutes covers slicing the potatoes, onion and chard, skinning the fish and whisking, and the 30 cook minutes match the hob and baking times.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning appears in the steps, nothing unlisted is used, and the names match their ids.

seasonal_feel.reason: A generous 300g of chard with new potatoes and dill makes a fitting early-June lunch, and the chard is central rather than a garnish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with sensible cues such as 'until the edges start to set'.

hearty_healthy.reason: Eggs, fish, potatoes and greens served with salad make a balanced, filling lunch a family would happily eat.
